title: Length-Harmonized Microbatching with Interleaved Prefill/Decode Scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our serving traces show that end-to-end token cost and tail latency are driven by worst-case padding in microbatches. Current bucketing uses coarse seqlen bins which either overpad short requests or fragment capacity for long requests. We also observe suboptimal kernel choices for heterogeneous microbatches and stalls during the transition between prefill and decode phases. Goal: Build a runtime component that harmonizes microbatch lengths, reduces padding, and schedules interleaved prefill/decode in a way that (1) keeps SLOs for tail latency, (2) reduces per-token GPU cost by 8-15% for mixed workloads, and (3) produces stable kernel-selection signals for the kernel selector/oracle.
goals: Reduce average padded tokens per request by 20-40% compared to current coarse bucketing
Limit 95th percentile latency regression to <= 5% vs baseline for our 99ms SLO use-case
Provide stable kernel-cost estimates to kernel selector to avoid oscillation during rollouts
Enable graceful priority handling for low-latency premium traffic (dedicated tier)
design_decisions: Length Harmonizer: group incoming requests into 'harmonized slabs' that accept a small adjustable stretch factor instead of fixed-length bins. A slab has a target_length and an allowed stretch (e.g., +/- 12%).

Soft-Slab Packing: when slab is not full, allow short requests to be stretched (by trimming low-entropy prefixes or using prefill coalescing heuristics) to improve GPU efficiency while preserving output quality metrics.

Interleaved Prefill/Decode Scheduler: instead of strict prefill-all then decode-all, interleave decode work for earlier-ready requests to improve throughput and reduce tail latency for short responses.

Kernel-Cost Oracle: use a lightweight online estimator that combines static model kernels' cost table with sampled microbatch measurements to pick kernels at slab boundaries and avoid per-request kernel thrash.
KV Prefix Coalescer: coalesce identical or similar prefixes within a slab to avoid redundant KV storage and reduce memory traffic during prefill.
Backpressure & Preemption: implement decode-signal-aware preemption that pauses low-priority decoding to admit new prefill work if slab latency budget would be violated.
algorithm: 1) On request arrival, place request in an ingress queue with its seqlen and priority metadata.

2) Periodically form candidate slabs (100ms window or size cap) by greedy packing into nearest target_length slab if within stretch; otherwise create new slab. Preference for coalescing similar prefix hashes.
3) For each slab: compute kernel selection using kernel-cost oracle (static cost + recent runtime samples). Pin kernel for the slab to avoid oscillation during execution.
4) Start prefill for slab; while waiting for slower prefill rows, opportunistically schedule decode work for requests whose prefix KV is ready and whose decode budget remains within slab latency SLO.
5) If slab can't meet latency budget, invoke decode preemption to prioritize earlier completions and spill remaining requests to next scheduling round.
6) Emit slab telemetry: padded_tokens, kernel_selected, decode_preemptions, latency_p95, cost_estimate.
metrics: Throughput: tokens/sec per-GPU for mixed workload traces
Cost: GPU-ms or token-cost per 1k requests
Quality: model output divergence pre/post harmonizer on canned eval prompts
experiment_plan: Stage 0 - Simulation: run harmonizer offline against one month of production trace. Produce padded token and latency deltas and simulate kernel oracle behavior.
Stage 1 - Canary (internal): enable on 5% of host pool for internal traffic with feature flag; collect telemetry for 48h and measure decode preemption events and kernel selection stability.
Stage 2 - Customer Canary: route low-priority customer traffic (non-critical, trial orgs) with monitoring alerts; validate no >5% latency regressions for premium orgs.
Stage 3 - Rollout: ramp in 10/25/50/100% with automated rollback if customer_impact or latency SLOs exceed thresholds.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Simulation shows >=20% padded token reduction for mixed short/long workload trace
2) Canary 48h: p95 latency regression <=5% for production traffic; no SLA violations for premium traffic
3) Kernel selection thrash reduced to <2 changes/min per worker compared to baseline
4) No measurable quality regression on canonical eval set (ROUGE/BLEU/divergence thresholds pre-agreed with ML team)
5) Observability dashboards and alerts created and tested
risks: Stretch heuristics may alter model outputs for some prompts — mitigate via prefix-preserving fallbacks and eval gating
Kernel oracle inaccuracies at cold-start could pick suboptimal kernels — mitigate with short-lived sampling and conservative pinning
Prefill/decode interleaving complexity may introduce deadlocks if preemption isn't correctly engineered — need rigorous integration tests
Increased scheduler CPU/coordination overhead may reduce net GPU gains for very high QPS clusters — add CPU budget guardrails
